public_rationale: He said his roughly two years of data showed no period of cost-cutting at Anthropic, only rising monthly spending. His AWS bills are not public. Anthropic's S-1, filed 26 October 2026, is the best stand-in: it covers compute spending across all cloud providers. It says compute and infrastructure spending rose every quarter, from $944M in Q1 2025 to $2,047M in Q3 2025. For the full year 2025 it rose 190% over 2024. No quarter in the window shows a cut. One part cuts the other way. Operating cash burn fell from $5.69B in 2024 to $2.64B in 2025, and the filing says that was mainly because prepaid hosting was being used up, not because spending fell. Read as being about costs, which is what his data covered, the claim holds. Read as net cash burn, it would be mixed.
limitations: The S-1 compute figures cover all cloud providers, not just AWS.
There is no quarterly breakdown for 2024.
The result depends on reading 'burns' as spending rather than net cash flow.

from_speaker: "no period of time that I can see"
"just under two years of data I've been party to"
"any means of — or any success doing — cost-cutting"
"the only thing this company seems capable of doing is increasing the amount of money it burns on a monthly basis"
our_interpretation: Plain reading: during the roughly two years his data covers (about January 2024 to September 2025), Anthropic's compute and infrastructure spending never fell. It kept rising, with no period of cost reduction.

His data was Anthropic's AWS bills, which are not public. The closest public measure is the 'compute and infrastructure' cost line in Anthropic's S-1 filing. It covers all cloud providers, not just AWS, and is used as a stand-in.

'Burns' is read as spending, mainly on compute, because that is the data his statement rests on. It is not read as net operating cash flow, which also moves with prepayments and payment timing. Cash-flow evidence is reported as counterevidence.
The S-1 gives quarterly figures only from Q1 2025. Data for 2024 is annual only.
A falling share of costs to revenue is not cost-cutting under this reading; the test is whether costs themselves fell.
criteria.support_condition: Public financial data for about January 2024 to September 2025 shows Anthropic's compute and infrastructure spending rising period after period, with no period of absolute reduction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Public data shows Anthropic's compute and infrastructure spending fell in absolute terms in some period between January 2024 and September 2025, or shows the company reporting deliberate cost reductions that lowered spending in that window.

Compute and infrastructure expenses increased sequentially in each of the quarters presented, from $944

evidence.locator: Quarterly Trends, Operating Expenses, Compute and Infrastructure (p. 158–159)
evidence.explanation: Anthropic's compute spending rose every quarter of 2025 within his window. The S-1 table shows $944M, $1,390M and $2,047M for Q1–Q3 2025. There was no quarter of reduction.

evidence.excerpt:
Compute and infrastructure expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $4.8 billion, or 190%,
compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.
evidence.locator: MD&A, Operating Expenses, Compute and Infrastructure (p. 151)
evidence.explanation: Compute spending nearly tripled from 2024 ($2,522M) to 2025 ($7,326M). This is consistent with costs rising across his window. The 2025 total includes Q4 2025, which falls outside it.

evidence.excerpt:
Net cash used in operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $3.1 billion compared
to the year ended December 31, 2024.
evidence.explanation: Operating cash burn fell from $5,692M (2024) to $2,637M (2025), and H1 2025 was $1,513M. If 'burns' means cash burn, this cuts against him. The filing attributes the fall to using up prepaid hosting and to payment timing, alongside rising cloud costs, not to cost-cutting.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Quarterly or monthly 2024 compute spending, or Anthropic's AWS-specific bills, would confirm or overturn the 2024 part of the window.
